architecturalPlan.scaleRationale: A $25 million brief is resolved as a highly crafted, single-level 1,024 m² courtyard residence rather than an inflated acreage exercise. Its value is concentrated in a long ceremonial gallery, generously proportioned public rooms, three fully realised bedroom domains, deep outdoor living, a formal pool court, limestone-and-bronze detailing, and independently articulated roof planes. The deliberately compact one-level arrangement provides step-free living and makes every major room engage the pool court while preserving the estate-like arrival sequence.
architecturalPlan.arrivalAndCirculation: Level 0 walking-surface datum is Y=0.20 m. Arrival approaches the west-facing bronze entrance in the long limestone gallery at X=-4.00. The 4 m-wide gallery is the primary circulation spine: it connects the salon, dining room, kitchen, primary suite and both guest suites through actual openings in its east wall. The pool court is reached from the north-facing glazed public-room elevation. Internal stair geometry is not required because the residence is single level.
architecturalPlan.volumeHierarchy: The 18 x 14 m salon is the primary public volume, expressed with the highest and deepest flat roof plane. Dining and kitchen form a lower eastward service-and-entertaining bar. The 18 x 16 m primary suite is a quiet south volume, while two substantial guest suites form a secondary eastward sleeping bar. The narrow gallery is deliberately lower and reads as a sheltered arrival datum rather than a competing volume.
architecturalPlan.relationshipsAndViews: Level 0 plan tiles without overlap: gallery X=-4..0, Z=-16..14; salon X=0..18, Z=0..14; dining X=18..28, Z=0..14; kitchen X=28..40, Z=0..14; primary suite X=0..18, Z=-16..0; guest suite one X=18..28, Z=-16..0; guest suite two X=28..40, Z=-16..0. The shared boundary at X=0 is divided into gallery-to-primary and gallery-to-salon walls; the Z=0 crosswall divides public and private rooms. The north side opens onto a 40 x 18 m articulated pool terrace; a 14 x 6 m water basin is surrounded by separate walkable deck plates. The salon has the principal pool-facing outlook, with dining and kitchen extending the entertaining frontage.
architecturalPlan.roofFacadeAndMaterials: All ground slabs are 0.20 m thick with top walking surface at Y=0.20 m. Gallery enclosure rises from Y=0.20 to its roof underside at Y=3.20 m; its 0.30 m roof occupies Y=3.20..3.50 m. Secondary rooms rise to Y=3.35 m and receive 0.30 m roofs occupying Y=3.35..3.65 m. The salon rises to Y=3.85 m and its 0.35 m primary roof occupies Y=3.85..4.20 m. Limestone walls establish the heavy enclosure and framing piers; bronze is reserved for the recessed entrance and glazing frames; timber screens create shade at the public pool facade. Flat roofs have deep, deliberate overhangs, with the salon roof visibly more substantial than the subsidiary planes.

commitments.description: Recessed, sheltered west arrival is evidenced by the bronze entry door set into the gallery's dedicated entry opening.
The gallery is the legible horizontal circulation spine at the level-zero walking datum.
The salon is the dominant civic room and has the tallest roof datum.
The dining, kitchen, primary suite and guest suites are subordinate but complete residential volumes.
Layered flat roof planes distinguish gallery, secondary rooms and the principal salon.
The pool facade is composed as actual glazed openings within limestone enclosure, softened by timber shade screens.
The pool court is a walkable sequence of separately modelled deck plates around an explicit water basin.

result.name: Limestone Gallery Court
result.summary: A single-level, 1,024 m² luxury courtyard mansion organised around a ceremonial gallery and a long pool court. A high salon roof anchors the composition, while lower limestone sleeping and entertaining volumes create a calm, layered estate character.
unsupported: The site is temporarily represented as level ground at Y=0 in accordance with generation-site policy; no terrain, grading, planting, driveway, or landscape topography is modelled.
Internal furniture, bathrooms, cabinetry, stair/interior construction, MEP, structural engineering, code compliance, drainage, and pool excavation are not represented.
Curved or polygonal mansion shells, arbitrary mesh forms, and custom curved roofs are not supported by the available editable primitives.
